label: Cells and tissues may have something it is like to make decisions
claim: Because some nervous systems give rise to first-person experience and neural and non-neural networks differ minimally apart from time scale, it is natural to hypothesize that there is something it is like to be a tissue or organ making decisions, e.g. a pancreas may have as much proto-consciousness as a simple neural network.
quote: But, given that at least some nervous systems do give rise to such experience and that the differences between neural networks and non-neural ones (aside from temporal scale) are minimal, it is natural to hypothesize that there is something-it-is-like to being a tissue or organ and making decisions.
paper_title: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
section: What Does It Feel Like to be a Pancreas?
scope: Non-neural tissues and organs

label: Evolutionary algorithms can design novel living organisms built from frog cells
claim: A pipeline in which an evolutionary algorithm designs candidate organisms in silico for a desired function, and transferable designs are then built from Xenopus cells with a cell-based construction toolkit, can produce novel living systems that show the predicted behaviours, though some steps still need manual intervention.
quote: Here we show a scalable pipeline for creating functional novel lifeforms: AI methods automatically design diverse candidate lifeforms in silico to perform some desired function, and transferable designs are then created using a cell-based construction toolkit to realize living systems with the predicted behaviors.
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Abstract
scope: Xenopus laevis embryonic epidermal and cardiac progenitor tissue shaped into designed aggregates

label: Designed organisms moved as simulated when upright, much less when inverted
claim: For at least one deciliated, cardiac-muscle-powered design, the upright organisms' direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations, and inverting the design significantly reduced net displacement both in silico and in vivo.
quote: More specifically, the upright organisms’ direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations (P < 0.01; details in SI Appendix, section S9), and inverting the design significantly reduced its net displacement both in silico (P < 0.001) and in vivo (P < 0.0001).
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Results › Locomotion.
scope: Deciliated Xenopus reconfigurable organisms with cardiac tissue, compared with their simulated designs

label: Behaviour transfer from simulation to organism was due to the designed shape
claim: The authors interpret the orientation-dependent match between simulated and living organisms as showing that successful transfer of locomotion from simulation to the living organism was due to the designed morphology itself, not chance.
quote: This suggests that successful transference did not result by chance but rather was due to the design itself.
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Results › Locomotion.
scope: Evolved designs realized as Xenopus reconfigurable organisms

label: Motile designs spontaneously aggregate particles in simulation and in vivo
claim: When the environment contains particulate matter, motile designs spontaneously gather the particles into aggregates, both in simulation and as living Xenopus-cell organisms.
quote: When the environment is strewn with particulate matter, motile designs spontaneously aggregate the external objects both in silico (SI Appendix, Fig. S10) and in vivo (Fig. 3F and SI Appendix, Fig. S11).
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Results › Object Manipulation.
scope: Xenopus reconfigurable organisms and their simulated counterparts in a particle-strewn dish

label: Pairs of organisms collide, bond and orbit, more so with cilia active
claim: Collective behaviours predicted in simulation were observed in vivo: two organisms often collide, form a temporary mechanical bond and orbit each other for several revolutions before detaching, and this is more pronounced when cilia are not inhibited.
quote: For instance, two designs often collide, form a temporary mechanical bond, and orbit about each other for several revolutions before detaching along tangential trajectories (SI Appendix, Fig. S10). This phenomenon is more pronounced when cilia are not inhibited on the organisms
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Results › Collective Behavior.
scope: Multiple Xenopus reconfigurable organisms sharing a dish, with and without cilia

label: Selection for locomotion under random actuation evolved derandomizing shapes
claim: In the voxel-based soft-body simulation with randomly phased contractile cells, selection for locomotion produced morphologies that derandomize motion: shape and the distribution of passive and contractile cells evolved so the global movement was coherent despite random actuation.
quote: As a side effect of selection pressure for locomotion, derandomizing morphologies evolved: evolutionary improvement occurred through changes in overall shape, and distribution of the passive and contractile cells, to collectively derandomize the global movement produced by the random actuation.
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Discussion
scope: Evolutionary design in a soft-body physics simulation of passive and contractile voxels

label: Cell competence lets neural-less novel aggregates self-organize functionally
claim: The behavioural competence of individual cells and their propensity to cooperate in groups facilitate functional morphogenesis in novel circumstances, so that the designed organisms, despite lacking nervous systems, following novel developmental trajectories and mixing tissues, still possess self-organizing properties that support their designed behaviour.
quote: The behavioral competence of individual cells, and the propensity of cells to cooperate in groups, facilitate functional morphogenesis in novel circumstances. The lifeforms presented here, despite lacking nervous systems, following novel developmental trajectories, and being composed of materials from different tissues, nevertheless possess these self-organizing properties.
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Discussion
scope: Xenopus cells in novel, designed multicellular configurations

label: Cardiomyocytes in built organisms spontaneously made phase-matched contractions
claim: Although signalling between cardiomyocytes was not designed or enforced, cardiac muscle cells in the built organisms spontaneously coordinated to produce coherent, phase-matched contractions that aided locomotion.
quote: For instance, although signaling between cardiomyocytes was not enforced, emergent spontaneous coordination among the cardiac muscle cells produced coherent, phase-matched contractions which aided locomotion in the physically realized designs.
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Discussion
scope: Xenopus cardiac progenitor tissue embedded in reconfigurable organisms

label: Reconfigurable organisms self-repair, closing lacerations
claim: Reconfigurable organisms built from Xenopus cells maintain their externally imposed shape and also self-repair after damage, for example automatically closing lacerations.
quote: Finally, reconfigurable organisms not only self-maintain their externally imposed configuration, but they also self-repair in the face of damage, such as automatically closing lacerations (SI Appendix, Fig. S9).
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Discussion
scope: Xenopus laevis reconfigurable organisms

label: Adding hydrodynamics and random actuation made simulated gaits match living ones
claim: Designs first evolved on simulated land had bounding gaits that did not transfer to living organisms; adding first-order hydrodynamics and randomized phase offsets produced designs whose behaviour better matched the living systems, in contact with the ground for 93.3% of evaluation versus 52.7% on the first pass.
quote: The behavior of designs generated on the second pass better matched the behavior of the actual living systems: on average, designs were in contact with the ground plane for 93.3% of their evaluation period, compared to just 52.7% on the first pass (SI Appendix, section S6).
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Materials and Methods › Evolutionary Design.
scope: Soft-body voxel simulations of Xenopus reconfigurable organisms

label: Shape concavities of 100 µm or more persist in developing stem cell aggregates
claim: Aggregates of developing Xenopus pluripotent cells tend to close small gaps in their geometry; concavities 100 µm wide or more (12% of body length) gave stable long-term deformations, setting the minimal buildable feature size.
quote: Preliminary work determined that concavities with a width of 100 µm or greater (12% of total body length) produced stable long-term deformations suitable for biological building (SI Appendix, Fig. S7).
paper_title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
section: Materials and Methods › Build Filter.
scope: Reaggregated Xenopus laevis animal-cap tissue shaped by microsurgery

label: All known cognitive agents are collective intelligences made of agential parts
claim: Every known cognitive agent is a collective intelligence: biological agents are made of parts (cells and other components) that are themselves agents in important ways, and there is no truly indivisible cognitive being.
quote: All known cognitive agents are collective intelligences, because we are all made of parts; biological agents in particular are not just structurally modular, but made of parts that are themselves agents in important ways.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Introduction
scope: All known cognitive agents, especially multicellular organisms

label: Memories can persist through complete brain regeneration in planaria
claim: In some organisms such as planaria, memories (prior knowledge and behavioural tendencies) can apparently persist after the complete regeneration of the brain, being transferred onto the newly constructed brain.
quote: Not only that, but memories can apparently persist following the complete regeneration of brains in some organisms (McConnell et al., 1959; Corning, 1966; Shomrat and Levin, 2013) such as planaria, in which prior knowledge and behavioral tendencies are somehow transferred onto a newly-constructed brain.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Cognition: Changing the Subject
scope: Planarian flatworms trained before decapitation and head regeneration

label: Tadpoles with eyes on their tails can still perform visual learning
claim: Xenopus tadpoles engineered to have eyes on their tails instead of their heads are still readily able to perform visual learning tasks, illustrating that minds readily adapt to radically altered body architectures.
quote: When tadpoles are created to have eyes on their tails, instead of their heads, they are still readily able to perform visual learning tasks (Blackiston and Levin, 2013; Blackiston et al., 2017).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Cognition: Changing the Subject
scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with ectopic eyes transplanted to the tail and native eyes removed

label: Transitions in cognitive capacity are gradual, not binary
claim: Although major differences in cognitive function exist among diverse intelligences, transitions between them have not been shown to be binary or rapid relative to the timescale of individual agents; cognition-related properties form a continuum from humble proto-cognitive systems to advanced minds.
quote: Specifically, while major differences in cognitive function of course exist among diverse intelligences, transitions between them have not been shown to be binary or rapid relative to the timescale of individual agents.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences
scope: All cognitive systems across evolution, development and bioengineered hybrids

label: A system's level of agency must be determined empirically by prediction and control
claim: Under TAME, how much agency a system has is an empirical, observer-dependent question: the correct level of agency to attribute is the one whose model and intervention strategy give the most efficient prediction and control of the system, as established by experiment.
quote: Thus, the correct level of agency with which to treat any system must be determined by experiments that reveal which kind of model and strategy provides the most efficient predictive and control capability over the system.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences
scope: Any living, engineered or hybrid system

label: Gene regulatory network models exhibit associative learning
claim: Analyses of biological gene regulatory network models show that they exhibit associative and several other kinds of learning, as well as pattern completion and generalization, suggesting GRNs could be trained with patterned stimuli rather than rewired.
quote: Indeed, recent analyses of biological GRN models reveal that they exhibit associative and several other kinds of learning capacity, as well as pattern completion and generalization (Watson et al., 2010, 2014; Szilagyi et al., 2020; Biswas et al., 2021).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences
scope: Published ODE models of biological gene regulatory networks

label: A Self is marked by goals, compound memories and credit assignment above its parts
claim: TAME defines the hallmarks of a Self as the ability to pursue goals, to own compound (e.g. associative) memories, and to serve as the locus of credit assignment (reward or punishment), each at a scale larger than any of its components can achieve alone.
quote: The TAME framework takes the following as the basic hallmarks of being a Self: the ability to pursue goals, to own compound (e.g., associative) memories, and to serve as the locus for credit assignment (be rewarded or punished), where all of these are at a scale larger than possible for any of its components alone.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework
scope: Any agent, biological or engineered

label: The spatiotemporal scale of an agent's goals delineates its Self (cognitive light cone)
claim: Selves can be classified and compared by the spatio-temporal scale of the goals they can represent and work toward (their 'cognitive light cone'), and this scale delineates the boundaries of each Self.
quote: Specifically (Figure 4), a “space-time” diagram can be created where the spatio-temporal scale of any agent’s goals delineates that Self and its cognitive boundaries.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework
scope: Agents from microbes to humans and engineered systems

label: Stress binds distributed modules into one larger homeostatic loop
claim: Stress, defined as a system-level response to the difference between current state and a setpoint, scales Selves by binding modules that sense and act at different scales and locations into one global homeostatic loop; propagated stress signals recruit distant sub-agents to act so as to reduce their own stress.
quote: Stress is a systemic response to a difference between current state and a desired setpoint; it is an essential component to scaling of Selves because it enables different modules (which sense and act on things at different scales and in distributed locations) to be bound together in one global homeostatic loop (toward a larger purpose).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework
scope: Multicellular organisms and other multi-scale agents

label: Behavioural problem-solving in 3D space derives from older problem-solving in other spaces
claim: Problem-solving behaviour of animals in three-dimensional space is proposed to be a variant of an evolutionarily more ancient capacity to solve problems in metabolic, physiological, transcriptional and morphogenetic spaces.
quote: It is proposed that the traditional problem-solving behavior we see in standard animals in 3D space is just a variant of evolutionarily more ancient capacity to solve problems in metabolic, physiological, transcriptional, and morphogenetic spaces (as one possible sequential timeline along which evolution pivoted some of the same strategies to solve problems in new spaces).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework
scope: Evolution of problem-solving capacities across life

label: Planaria regenerate barium-insensitive heads after barium-induced head loss
claim: Planaria exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker, lose their heads but soon regenerate heads that are completely insensitive to barium, by transcriptionally regulating relatively few genes; the authors interpret this as cells navigating transcriptional space to solve a novel physiological stressor not met in evolution.
quote: For example, when planaria are exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker, their heads explode. Remarkably, they soon regenerate heads that are completely insensitive to barium (Emmons-Bell et al., 2019).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework
scope: Planarian flatworms chronically exposed to barium chloride

label: Picasso tadpoles with scrambled faces become largely normal frogs
claim: Xenopus tadpoles whose craniofacial organs were placed in abnormal positions ('Picasso tadpoles') tend to become largely normal frogs, because the organs move along novel, abnormal paths and stop at the correct frog-face positions, showing that craniofacial remodelling is goal-directed rather than hardwired.
quote: Amazingly, they tend to turn into largely normal frogs because the craniofacial organs move in novel, abnormal paths [sometimes overshooting and needing to return a bit (Pinet et al., 2019)] and stop when they get to the correct frog face positions.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Goal-Directed Activity in Morphogenesis
scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with experimentally scrambled craniofacial organs undergoing metamorphosis

label: Deer antler trophic memory is a rewritable pattern memory
claim: In deer, a wound made on a branched antler in one year leads to ectopic tines at the same location in later years after the antler is shed, which the author interprets as an experience-dependent, rewritable pattern memory in which the target morphology is rewritten without changing the genome.
quote: This is an example of experience-dependent, re-writable pattern memory, in which the target morphology (the setpoint for anatomical homeostasis) is re-written within standard hardware.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops
scope: Antlered deer (Cervidae) after antler injury

label: Altering planarian voltage patterns changes head number and head species-shape
claim: In planaria, manipulating the endogenous bioelectric voltage pattern by targeting gap junctions or ion channels can produce worms with one, two or zero heads, or with head and brain shapes resembling other extant planarian species.
quote: Manipulation of the normal voltage pattern by targeting the gap junctions (Sordillo and Bargmann, 2021) or ion channels can give rise to planaria with one, two, or 0 heads, or heads with shape (and brain shape) resembling other extant species of planaria (Emmons-Bell et al., 2015; Sullivan et al., 2016).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops
scope: Regenerating planarian fragments (e.g. Dugesia japonica) treated with gap-junction or ion-channel modulators

label: Two-headed planarian state persists through further cutting despite wild-type genome
claim: Planaria with abnormal head number induced by transient bioelectric manipulation are permanently altered: when cut into pieces with no further treatment, the pieces continue to regenerate with abnormal head number despite wild-type genetics.
quote: Remarkably, the worms with abnormal head number are permanently altered to this pattern, despite their wild-type genetics: cut into pieces with no further manipulations, the pieces continue to regenerate with abnormal head number (Oviedo et al., 2010; Durant et al., 2017).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops
scope: Planarians after transient gap-junction blockade (e.g. octanol) and serial amputation

label: Transient bioelectric states can rewrite false pattern memories in animals
claim: Modulating a transient bioelectric state is a conserved mechanism by which false pattern memories (altered target morphologies) can be written into the genetically specified electrical circuits of a living animal, analogous to incepting false behavioural memories in brains with optogenetics.
quote: Thus, much like the optogenetic techniques used to incept false behavioral memories into brains (Vetere et al., 2019), modulation of transient bioelectric state is a conserved mechanism by which false pattern memories can be re-written into the genetically-specified electrical circuits of a living animal.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops
scope: Regenerating animals, chiefly planaria

label: Newt kidney tubules keep correct lumen size when cell size changes
claim: Newt kidney tubules normally made of 8 to 10 cells in cross-section are built from fewer cells when cell size is experimentally enlarged, and from a single cell wrapping around itself when cells are made very large, showing that different molecular mechanisms (cell-cell interactions vs cytoskeletal deformation) can be deployed to reach the same anatomical outcome.
quote: Even more remarkable than the scaling of the cell number to unexpected size changes (on an ontogenetic, not evolutionary, timescale) is the fact that if the cells are made really huge, just one cell wraps around itself and still makes a proper lumen (Figure 6D).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Multi-Scale Competency of Growth and Form
scope: Polyploid newt larvae (Fankhauser's experiments)

label: Injury to one limb can be read out from the opposite limb within 30 seconds
claim: Limbs show mirror-neuron-like and somatotopic responses to injury outside the nervous system: the type and site of damage to one limb can be read out within 30 seconds by imaging the opposite, uninjured limb.
quote: For example, mirror neurons and somatotopic representation are seen in limbs’ response to injury, where the type and site of damage to one limb can be read out within 30 s from imaging the opposite, un-injured limbs (Busse et al., 2018).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Specific Parallels Between Morphogenesis and Basal Cognition
scope: Xenopus tadpole limbs (Busse et al., 2018)

label: Genes for morphogenesis and for learning and memory should overlap widely
claim: TAME predicts significant and specific overlap between genes involved in morphogenesis and genes in memory and learning categories, beyond the known shared ion channels, connexins and neurotransmitter machinery; it also predicts that memory genes will appear in genetic studies of cancer, regeneration and embryogenesis.
quote: Significant and specific overlap are predicted for genes involved in morphogenesis and cognition (categories of memory and learning).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Not Just Philosophy: Why These Parallels Matter
scope: Gene sets across animals, testable by bioinformatics

label: Morphogenesis should be trainable by reinforcement for specific anatomical outcomes
claim: TAME predicts (not yet tested) that the collective intelligence of tissues may be trainable by reinforcement learning, using rewards and punishments such as nutrients, endorphins or shock, to produce specific morphological or gene-expression outcomes.
quote: Another key prediction that remains to be tested (ongoing in our lab) is trainability of morphogenesis. The collective intelligence of tissues could be sophisticated enough to be trainable via reinforcement learning for specific morphological outcomes.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Not Just Philosophy: Why These Parallels Matter
scope: Regenerating or developing animal tissues; clinical settings

label: Voltage-sensitive channels and gap junctions form rewritable dynamical memories
claim: Because ion channels and gap junctions are themselves voltage-sensitive, a transient voltage state can trigger progressive depolarization or gap-junction closure, so non-neural bioelectric circuits readily form dynamical-system memories that store information and change computation without changing the channel or junction hardware.
quote: The fact that a transient voltage state passing through a cell can set off a cycle of progressive depolarization (like an action potential) or gap junctional (GJ) closure means that such circuits readily form dynamical systems memories which can store different information and change their computational behavior without changing the hardware
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Non-neural Bioelectricity: What Bodies Think About
scope: Non-neural cell networks coupled by voltage-gated channels and gap junctions

label: Gap junctions merge cells into a larger Self by erasing signal ownership
claim: Because signals passing through gap junctions carry no marker of their cell of origin, gap-junctional coupling partially erases informational (memory) boundaries between cells, which promotes the formation of a larger Self whose parts work toward common goals.
quote: Thus, this property of GJ coupling promotes the creation of a larger Self by partially erasing the mnemic boundaries between the parts which might impair their ability to work toward a common goal.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self
scope: Gap-junction-coupled cell collectives in metazoan tissues

label: Cancer is a shrinking of the Self after gap junction closure
claim: Oncogene expression and carcinogen exposure close gap junctions, and the consequence is transformation to cancer, in which cells revert to unicellular-like selves, shrink their computational boundaries and treat the rest of the body as external environment.
quote: Indeed this occurs in cancer, where oncogene expression and carcinogen exposure leads to a closure of GJs (Vine and Bertram, 2002; Leithe et al., 2006). The consequence of this is transformation to cancer, where cells revert to their ancient unicellular selves (Levin, 2021b)—shrinking their computational boundaries and treating the rest of the body as external environment.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self
scope: Metazoan cells undergoing oncogenic transformation

label: Managing bioelectric connectivity induces or suppresses cancer independent of genetics
claim: Managing bioelectric connectivity between cells can override genetically determined states, inducing metastatic melanoma in a wild-type background or suppressing tumorigenesis driven by strong oncogenes such as p53 or KRAS mutations, so genetic alterations are not necessary either to induce or to revert cancer.
quote: Indeed, recent data show that managing this connectivity can override default genetically-determined states, inducing metastatic melanoma in a perfectly wild-type background (Blackiston et al., 2011) or suppressing tumorigenesis induced by strong oncogenes like p53 or KRAS mutations (Chernet and Levin, 2013a,b).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos (melanocyte conversion and oncogene-induced tumour-like structures)

label: Developmental bioelectricity preceded and gave rise to nervous systems
claim: Developmental bioelectrics is an ancient precursor of nervous systems: evolution first used analog bioelectric dynamics to position body configuration in developmental morphospace, long before some cells specialized in fast digital spiking to control behaviour in 3D space.
quote: Evolution first exploited this to enable cell groups to position the body configuration in developmental morphospace, long before some cells specialized to use very fast, digital spiking as neural networks for control of behavior as movement in 3-dimensional space (Fields et al., 2020).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems
scope: Evolution of bioelectric signalling and nervous systems in animals

label: Context-sensitive ion channels appear alongside complex metazoan body plans
claim: Ion channel phylogeny is ancient (many channel families likely predate the most recent unicellular ancestor of animals), and the appearance of context-sensitive channels enabling new bioelectric feedback loops tracks the appearance of complex body plans at the emergence of metazoa, indicating an evolutionary continuum from single-cell excitability to cognition via somatic pattern control.
quote: The phylogeny of ion channels is ancient, and the appearance of context-sensitive channels (enabling new kinds of bioelectrical feedback loops) tracks well with the appearance of complex body plans at the emergence of metazoa (Moran et al., 2015), revealing the remarkable evolutionary continuum that leads from membrane excitability in single cells to cognitive functions in advanced organisms, by way of somatic pattern control (Cook et al., 2014).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems
scope: Ion channel gene families across unicellular eukaryotes and early-branching metazoans

label: A single ion channel can induce complete ectopic eyes where Pax6 cannot
claim: In Xenopus, the action of a single ion channel can induce an eye-specific bioelectric state that creates complete eyes in gut endoderm, spinal cord and posterior tissues, locations where genetic master regulators such as Pax6 are insufficient in vertebrates; bioelectric states thus act as master regulators that evolution can exploit for modular anatomical change.
quote: For example, the action of a single ion channel can induce an eye-specific bioelectric state that creates complete eyes in gut endoderm, spinal cord, and posterior tissues (Pai et al., 2012)—locations where genetic “master regulators” like the Pax6 transcription factor are insufficient in vertebrates (Chow et al., 1999).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos misexpressing ion channels

label: Mutations in electrogenic genes can produce coordinated, long-range anatomical change
claim: Because the same membrane-voltage dynamics can be produced by many ion-channel combinations and bioelectric states act across tissue distances, evolution can swap channels freely, and simple mutations in electrogenic genes can cause long-range, highly coordinated changes in anatomy (supported by KCNH8 and a connexin in an evolutionary shift of fish fin morphology).
quote: evolution is free to swap out channels and explore the bioelectrical state space: simple mutations in electrogenic genes can exert very long-range, highly coordinated changes in anatomy.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems
scope: Animal morphological evolution, e.g. fish fins

label: Multiscale competency shields mutations from selection and smooths fitness landscapes
claim: In organisms with a multiscale competency architecture, whose modules actively correct toward a target morphology, mutations that would be detrimental in hardwired organisms (e.g. displacing the eye) become neutral, so the architecture shields some of mutations' negative effects from selection and smooths the fitness landscape.
quote: Thus, MCA shields from selection some aspects of mutations’ negative effects (which inevitably are the bulk of random mutations’ consequences).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Evolutionary Aspects › Multi-Scale Autonomy Potentiates the Speed of Evolution
scope: Evolving multicellular organisms; computational models of evolution with competent cells

label: Anatomical homeostasis may exist mainly to correct mutation-induced deviations
claim: The primary reason for anatomical homeostasis in regulative development and regeneration may be to correct deviations from target morphology caused by mutations, rather than to repair damage.
quote: The primary reason for the anatomical homeostasis seen in regulative development and regeneration may be for dealing, not with damage, but with deviations from target morphology induced by mutations.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Evolutionary Aspects › Multi-Scale Autonomy Potentiates the Speed of Evolution
scope: Evolution of regulative development and regeneration in animals

label: Systems operating in morphogenetic or transcriptional spaces have minimal consciousness
claim: TAME provisionally holds that consciousness comes in degrees and that embodiment includes perception-action systems in any space, implying that systems operating in morphogenetic, transcriptional and other spaces should have some, if very minimal, degree of consciousness.
quote: This implies, counter to many people’s intuitions, that systems that operate in morphogenetic, transcriptional, and other spaces should also have some (if very minimal) degree of consciousness.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Consciousness
scope: Tissues, cell collectives and other non-neural systems

label: General anesthetics block gap junctions, dissolving the higher-level Self
claim: General anesthetics are gap-junction blockers, and on TAME's account shutting down electrical communication between cells makes the higher-level computational layer (the larger Self) disappear while the cells remain healthy; gap-junction blockers anesthetize organisms ranging from plants and Hydra to humans.
quote: Interestingly, general anesthetics are gap junction blockers (Wentlandt et al., 2006): consistent with the cognitive scaling example above, shutting down electrical communication among the cells leads to a disappearance of the higher-level computational layer while the cellular network is disrupted.
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Consciousness
scope: Anesthetized plants, Hydra and animals including humans

label: Briefly gap-junction-blocked planaria make other species' heads, then revert
claim: Planaria briefly treated with a gap-junction blocker regenerate heads shaped like those of other planarian species but eventually remodel back to their correct species-specific target morphology, which the author takes as parallel to the temporary loss and return of the Self under anesthesia.
quote: Interestingly, and in line with the proposed isomorphism between cognition and morphogenesis, gap junction blockade has exactly this effect in regeneration: planaria briefly treated with GJ blocker regenerate heads of other species, but eventually snap out of it and remodel back to their correct target morphology (Emmons-Bell et al., 2015).
paper_title: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
section: Consciousness
scope: Girardia dorotocephala planarian fragments treated with octanol
